$comment: The ES-surface probe corpus: the single source of truth for the T4 audit.
Consumed by audit.php (runs every probe against the committed guest fixture)
and by verify-proposal.mjs (type-checks every `check` source under the current
and the proposed compiler pin, using the same TypeScript 6.0.3 the guest embeds).
es      the ES revision that introduced the feature
lib     the lib .d.ts that declares it (the file the raise pulls in)
kind    runtime  - evaluated with `// @ts-nocheck`, must equal `expect`
raw      - evaluated verbatim (hashbang must be the first byte)
absent   - the engine does NOT have it; `expect` records how it fails
source  the JS/TS evaluated in the guest
expect  the exact value the guest must return
check   the TypeScript the checker sees (no @ts-nocheck); defaults to `source`.
audit.php --parity ALSO evaluates it, so it must be runnable, not
merely well-typed: a snippet that throws for its own reasons would
read as a checker/engine parity breach.
note    anything the raw verdict does not say by itself

const plain = new SharedArrayBuffer(8); const ctor = (() => { try { new SharedArrayBuffer(8, { maxByteLength: 16 }); return 'ok' } catch (e) { return e.constructor.name + ':' + e.message } })(); const grow = (() => { try { plain.grow(12); return 'ok' } catch (e) { return e.constructor.name + ':' + e.message } })(); plain.growable + ':' + plain.maxByteLength + ':' + ctor + ':' + grow
